Three Tanjong Pagar conservation shophouses up for sale at $43 mil
article:
A portfolio of three conservation shophouses at 83, 91 and 97 Tanjong Pagar Road has been put up for sale at a combined guide price of $43 million, or about $3,800 psf based on their total floor area.

Located within the Tanjong Pagar Conservation Area in District 2, the three commercially zoned shophouses have a combined land area of approximately 4,022 sq ft and a total floor area of 11,306 sq ft.

Both 83 and 91 Tanjong Pagar Road are three-storey conservation shophouses with attics, while 97 Tanjong Pagar Road is a two-storey shophouse with an attic.

The guide prices for 83 and 91 Tanjong Pagar Road are $14.5 million each, while 97 Tanjong Pagar Road has a guide price of $14 million.

The seller, Strathmore Management, acquired the three shophouses in separate transactions in 2021, based on caveats lodged.

Strathmore purchased 91 Tanjong Pagar Road for $10.5 million in May 2021, followed by 97 Tanjong Pagar Road for $10 million in September and 83 Tanjong Pagar Road for $11.3 million in October that year.

The combined purchase price was $31.8 million, compared with the current guide price of $43 million, representing a premium of 35.2% over the acquisition cost five years ago.

All three shophouses are on 99-year leases commencing in 1992, with approximately 65 years remaining. They are fully tenanted to a mix of established F&B, retail, lifestyle and wellness operators, as well as professional services firms.

At 91 Tanjong Pagar Road, the ground floor is occupied by bespoke jewellery retailer Michael Trio, while Korean fusion restaurant Kream Korea occupies the ground floor of 83 Tanjong Pagar Road. The ground-floor tenant at 97 Tanjong Pagar Road is Peranakan restaurant Blue Ginger.

According to CBRE, several of the tenants are long-standing occupiers, providing recurring rental income for prospective buyers.

Once known for traditional businesses and bridal shops, Tanjong Pagar has evolved into a bustling dining and lifestyle destination, with an eclectic mix of restaurants, cafés, bars, and speciality retailers. The precinct also benefits from the working population of nearby office developments such as Guoco Tower , International Plaza and Frasers Tower .

"Conservation shophouses in Tanjong Pagar are tightly held and seldom come to market, let alone three at once with prime frontage along Tanjong Pagar Road," says Clemence Lee, executive director of capital markets, Singapore, at CBRE.

He adds that the properties are well maintained and fully occupied, offering investors immediate rental income with minimal leasing risk.

The shophouses are within a 10-minute walk of Tanjong Pagar, Maxwell and Outram Park MRT stations. As commercially zoned properties, they are open to foreign buyers and companies, with no additional buyer's stamp duty (ABSD) payable.

CBRE is marketing the three properties through an expression of interest (EOI) exercise, which closes on Nov 26 at 3pm. Buyers can submit offers for the entire portfolio or individual shophouses.

title: Sea Limited Stock: Is the Southeast Asian Tech Giant Making a Comeback?
article:
Sea Limited
(NYSE: SE) – often perceived as one of the crown jewels of the Southeast Asian tech space – was propelled to dizzying heights as lockdown-fuelled demand for online gaming and e-commerce peaked during the pandemic.
Eventually, reality set in, as rising global interest rates, the unexpected ban on its flagship game
Free Fire
in India, and costly international missteps in markets like Argentina threw a spanner in the works for its premium valuations.
Sea’s share price fell as much as 90% from its peak, as investors who bought near the top rushed to exit with brutal losses.
After aggressive belt-tightening and a series of operational restructuring that swung its bottom line into the green, is the comeback underway for Sea Limited?
Staging A Comeback with Three Profit Engines
In the second quarter of 2026 (2Q2026), Sea’s group GAAP revenue rose 48.1% year on year (YoY) to US$7.8 billion, driving net income up 10.6% to US$458.1 million.
The reason?
A robust digital ecosystem powered by a trio of interconnected businesses: e-commerce platform Shopee, digital entertainment provider Garena, and fintech operator Monee.
This ecosystem is anchored by Shopee.
Having invested heavily in local pickup stations and same-day delivery, Shopee has built logistics efficiency its competitors struggle to match.
That gives it a credible physical moat that maintains its 53% regional market share.
Shopee’s 2Q2026 GAAP take rate rose 200 basis points YoY to 14.6%, underscoring its growing bargaining power with merchants.
With management optimistic that Shopee will reach US$1 billion in adjusted EBITDA for FY2026, Shopee shows no signs of slowing down.
Garena’s 2Q2026 GAAP revenue surged 33.5% YoY to US$747 million, driving adjusted EBITDA up 16.8% to US$430 million.
Notably, this segment is the largest profit contributor by adjusted EBITDA, with Shopee at US$255.4 million and Monee at US$288.0 million.
However, most of Garena’s revenue is contributed by just one battle-royale hit,
Free Fire
, raising questions about the segment’s long-term sustainability.
Monee, Sea’s high-growth digital financial services arm, saw its 2Q2026 revenue climb 58.9% YoY to US$1.4 billion, while adjusted EBITDA rose 12.8% YoY to US$288.0 million.
But Monee couldn’t have achieved this momentum on its own.
Shopee’s proprietary consumer shopping data enables Monee to offer consumers greater payment flexibility through Buy-Now-Pay-Later (BNPL) while keeping its non-performing loan (NPL) ratio at 1.0%, comparable to those of Singapore
banks
.
Related articles:
Sea Limited in 2026: Is It Finally Time to Treat It Like a “Blue Chip”?
Is Sea Limited Still a Growth Story or Value Trap?
What Can Go Wrong with Its Comeback
With its recent operational recovery, Sea’s comeback looks sustainable.
Or is it?
There are a few reasons the storm might not be over yet.
Shopee dominates traditional e-commerce, where consumers search for what they want.
But more buying now happens through live-streams and short videos.
This ‘content commerce’ made up 32% of Southeast Asia’s online sales in 2025, up from 20% in 2024, according to Momentum Works.
TikTok Shop, built on a highly engaging video app, could have the long-term edge here.
Shopee isn’t standing still: live-stream and short-video orders now make up over 25% of its physical-goods orders in Southeast Asia.
The rise of agentic AI is also a wild card for Sea’s growth.
If shoppers start relying on AI agents, such as Muse from
Meta Platforms
(NASDAQ: META), to compare prices, Shopee’s fast-growing advertising revenue could be disrupted.
Founder Forrest Li has been instrumental in guiding Sea through a tough turnaround.
However, Li holds 57.6% of Sea’s total voting power, giving him effective control of the company.
And with the turnaround so closely tied to Li, his eventual departure would be a major event – Sea itself flags its reliance on key management as a risk.
Sea’s S$50 million pledge to Singapore football in March 2026 may raise questions about whether such “side quests” distract management.
Still, to put this pledge into perspective, S$50 million is a drop in the ocean Sea Limited’s S$3.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents as of 30 June 2026, giving investors little reason to be alarmed.
Geopolitically, Chinese
tech behemoth
Tencent’s stake in Sea could expose it to political friction in key overseas markets, as evidenced by India’s banning of Free Fire over China security worries.
Related articles:
If You Invested $10,000 Into Sea Limited at Its IPO, Here’s What It’s Worth Now
Sea Limited’s Path to Profitability: Can Shopee Keep Leading E-Commerce?
Get Smart: Anchoring Your Investment Expectations
Sea Limited has evolved from speculative pandemic hype into a self-sustaining digital ecosystem with multiple growth engines.
Its share trades at a price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of about 2.11 times.
Local investors can also buy
Sea Limited
(SGX: UGGD) on SGX through
Singapore Depository Receipts
(SDR), which represents shares listed overseas.
If the group’s earnings miss market expectations, investors should be prepared to endure wild price swings.
With no dividend payouts to cushion these potential downturns, Sea remains an aggressive stock to own, better suited as a manageable, a small satellite holding alongside a well-diversified core portfolio.

title: CLI appoints Hsieh Fu Hua as chairman of the board; Temasek’s Png Chin Yee joins the board as director
article:
CapitaLand Investment (CLI) has appointed Hsieh Fu Hua as independent chairman and non-executive independent director of the board. Hsieh, the former CEO of Singapore Exchange (SGX), joined CLI’s board as deputy chairman on Aug 12.

Png Chin Yee, president of Temasek Singapore, has also been appointed to CLI’s board as non-executive non-independent director.

Hsieh and Png will step into their roles from Jan 1, 2027.

Their appointments follow the retirement of Miguel Ko, CLI’s non-executive chairman and non-independent director, and Seviora CEO Gabriel Lim Meng Liang as non-executive and non-independent director. Ko and Lim will complete their respective terms on Dec 31.

“It is my privilege to be appointed chairman of CLI. On behalf of the board, I thank Miguel and Gabriel for their significant contributions, and welcome Chin Yee, whose extensive experience will strengthen the board,” says Hsieh.

“As CLI enters its next phase, our CEO, Lee Chee Koon, has my full support. I look forward to working closely with him and the management team to address our strategic priorities and execute them with discipline,” he adds.

See also: National Parks Board chairman one of two new independent non-executive directors appointed to ComfortDelGro’s board

Upon his retirement, Ko would have served 12 years with the group, from his appointment as CEO of Ascendas-Singbridge in 2014 to his current role. Lim will have served the board for over nine years, following his appointment to board of CapitaLand Limited in 2017.

“It has been a privilege to serve as chairman of CLI and contribute to its transformation and growth. Since its listing, CLI has built a differentiated, globally integrated real asset management platform anchored in Asia, underpinned by disciplined execution of its asset-light growth strategy,” says Ko.

“I am grateful to my fellow board members, management and colleagues for their commitment and contributions. Fu Hua brings deep experience, wisdom and sound judgement to the role. I am confident that, under his stewardship and with the continued support of the board and our talented leadership team, CLI will grow to greater heights,” he adds.

Shares in CLI closed 2 cents lower or 0.86% down at $2.31 on Oct 22.

title: Spotify keeps adding users in 3Q but misses slightly on revenue
article:
(Oct 22): Spotify Technology SA reported monthly active users grew 1% in the third quarter (3Q), over the prior quarter, to reach 788 million while its paying subscribers increased 2% to hit 306 million, meeting analysts’ expectations for total users, though slightly missing on subscribers, according to Bloomberg consensus.

Investors had been expecting 305 million paying customers and 788 million users in total.

Total revenue in the three months ending in September climbed to €4.97 billion, the company said on Thursday, up 16% over the prior year and slightly missing Wall Street’s projections of €4.98 billion.

Advertising-specific revenue increased more slowly to €482 million, missing estimates of €484.8 million. Ad sales have long been a challenge for the company, which has struggled to turn the segment into a meaningful business despite having more free users than paying subscribers.

During the past quarter, Spotify announced plans to expand its audiobook business. Audiobooks, which the company says drives revenue — especially for super users who pay extra to receive more hours of listening — are coming to new markets, including Spain, Mexico and Norway.

The company’s podcast efforts, which are now increasingly focused on a limited number of big shows, received a boost through a deal renewal with Joe Rogan, effectively giving Spotify the rights to sell advertising on his podcast, which remains the top-rated show in the US. The company also works with Amy Poehler on her podcast and has a deal with Netflix Inc to distribute certain shows on the streamer.

See also: Former Hungarian central bank governor detained, says report

Gross margin in 3Q came in at 33%, exactly hitting analysts’ estimates for the metric.

The company has continued to sign music deals with record labels and publishers to build its forthcoming artificial intelligence-powered remixing tool, which will let users pay more to customise songs to their liking. Spotify faces growing competition from a slew of startups that are looking to build similar features.

The company forecast €5.2 billion in revenue for the fourth quarter and 818 million monthly users, both largely in line with analysts’ estimates.

title: Indonesia eyes panda bond in November as it confronts MSCI risk — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 22): Indonesia is seeking to raise as much as 10 billion yuan through a panda bond sale, returning to China’s onshore debt market as Southeast Asia’s largest economy confronts MSCI Inc’s double downgrade threat.

Indonesian officials met with some investors in Shanghai on Thursday for the potential bond offering, according to people familiar with the matter. The bond, which could be marketed as early as next month, may have maturities of three, five and seven years, said the people, who asked not to be identified discussing private information.

The indicative size of the issuance is in the range of seven billion to 10 billion yuan, said Suminto, director general of budget financing and risk management at Indonesia’s Ministry of Finance, in response to a Bloomberg query. The issuance is planned for November through early December, he said.

“The cost of funds for panda bonds is relatively lower and China’s financial markets remain fairly stable amid current global financial market dynamics,” Suminto said. Issuing yuan-denominated debt supports the Indonesian government’s “efforts to diversify instruments and expand the investor base,” he added.

The planned panda debt sale is Indonesia’s second after a maiden offering in July when it raised seven billion yuan. It comes as Indonesia’s stock market is under pressure following MSCI’s warning that Indonesia’s emerging-market status was in jeopardy, fuelling concerns of potentially billions of dollars in capital outflows.

See also: Long-term Treasuries hold gains as oil snaps three-day rally

The benchmark Jakarta share index gained for a third straight day on Thursday after suffering its worst rout in nearly three decades last Friday. Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has said the country will not be “intimidated” by MSCI.

Emerging-market nations have been increasingly tapping China’s onshore bonds to reduce reliance on the US dollar and expand access to alternative pools of capital. Lower borrowing costs and a push to expand the yuan’s global use have fuelled a surge in panda bond sales this year. Issuance has reached nearly 250 billion yuan, already exceeding last year’s total of about 184 billion yuan, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

Indonesia sees opportunities for the yuan to play a broader role in its economy, from trade and investment transactions and eventually into financial and investment activities, Yulian Wihantoro, head of Bank Indonesia’s Beijing Representative Office, said at a forum in Beijing on Wednesday.

See also: DayOne in early talks with banks for potential US$500 mil bond — Bloomberg

The Southeast Asian nation has secured Chinese regulatory clearance to issue as much as 30 billion yuan of panda bonds from 2026 through 2028, a public filing shows. Its July issuance comprised of three-year notes at 1.9% and five-year notes at 2.19%.

Indonesia has already tapped international debt markets in multiple currencies this year, including the euro, yen and offshore yuan.

title: XMH Holdings to appeal $10.2 mil tax bill for FY2024; slapped with $12.5 mil tax for FY2025
article:
In bourse filings on Sept 18 and Oct 22, Mainboard-listed XMH Holdings has announced that the Indonesia tax authority has rejected its subsidiary PT Xin Ming Hua Engine’s (PT XMH) objection to an IDR143.9 billion ($10.2 million) tax bill for FY2024 ended April 30. As such, PT XMH will be filing formal appeals against the tax assessment.

The marine engine distributor has highlighted that should the full assessed amount for FY2024 be deemed payable, it would have a material financial impact on the XMH’s results for the current financial year.

XMH had first flagged the FY2024 tax bill on Sept 21, 2025. According to its annual report for financial year ended April 30, 2026, its independent tax advisor in Indonesia had considered the relevant facts, supporting documents and applicable tax regulations and advised that the FY2024 Indonesian tax assessment is without merit.

On a related note, the Indonesian tax authority had slapped PT XMH with a tax bill of approximately IDR 176.8 billion ($12.5 million) for FY2025 ended April 30, according to a Sept 4 bourse filing. The basis of the FY2025 Indonesian tax assessment is identical to that of FY2024’s notice.

PT XMH will similarly seek independent representation and advice from tax advisors in Indonesia on the FY2025 Indonesian tax bill. It says that it will explore all “available avenues” to satisfactorily resolve the issue, including but not limited to, the filing of a formal objection against the tax assessment notice.

Shares in XMH closed flat at 30 cents on Oct 22. The stock had completed a one-for-four share split on Sept 8 and had peaked at 59.75 cents on a pro-forma basis in late June.

See also: Christie’s International Real Estate launches in the Maldives

XMH Holdings announced $31.9 million in profit after tax for FY2026 ended April 30, in a bourse filing on June 26. This represented a y-o-y increase of almost 25%. Revenue increased by nearly 11% y-o-y to $185.3 million, while gross profit rose by 15.6% y-o-y to $63 million.

title: Copper slumps as surging stocks and tech-stock selloff sour mood
article:
(Oct 22): Copper slid as inventories on the London Metal Exchange (LME) surged for a second day and a selloff in AI-related stocks sapped risk appetite across global markets.

The red metal dropped as much as 2% to a low of US$14,076 a tonne, tracking losses in equities markets after earnings from major tech companies failed to reassure investors about the durability of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade. Copper has benefitted from that boom because of its use in data centers and power infrastructure.

The metal’s retreat from last month’s record high of US$14,875 a tonne has also been fuelled by doubts over whether the US will impose a tariff on refined copper as President Donald Trump approaches the midpoint of his second term. The prospect of a levy has drawn vast amounts of the metal into Comex exchange warehouses in the US this year, squeezing supplies on the LME.

Those supply constraints have caused spot copper prices to rally above futures over recent weeks, in a condition known as backwardation.

But on-warrant inventories have surged by 70,100 tonnes on the LME over the past two days, with the backwardation creating an incentive for stockholders to deliver metal against short positions, rather than rolling those hedges forward at a loss.

See also: Nickel rallies past US$16,000 on prospect of Indonesia output cuts

The bulk of the inflows were seen in the US, where futures prices on Comex have fallen to trade near parity with the LME over recent sessions. The collapse in the spread has come into sharp focus in the copper market, because it reduces the incentive to ship metal into the US and deliver it into Comex warehouses.

Even so, traders including Hartree Partners LP have built large positions in nearby LME contracts that could prove lucrative if tariffs are imposed, Bloomberg reported this week. If import duties are announced, traders could make a profit by buying near-dated LME contracts, and then withdrawing metal from LME warehouses in the US and delivering it against New York futures contracts once the new duties are implemented.

“There is still a great deal of uncertainty around next year’s copper supply-demand balance,” said Zhenting Zhou, a trader at Hangzhou Chenglian Industrial Co. “Mine supply should improve, US import demand is likely to ease, and China’s scrap-copper availability should also recover. There isn’t much upside risk for copper,” he said.

See also: Copper mines need US$332 bil new investment to ease shortfall

Still, some concerns remain around supply disruptions. Workers at Canada’s largest copper mine, Teck Resources Ltd’s Highland Valley Copper operation, are threatening to strike as early as Saturday, in the latest sign of labour tensions prompted by near-record prices that have emboldened employees to seek a greater share of profits.

Copper was 1.8% lower at US$14,105.50 a tonne on the LME as of 9.34am local time. Aluminium declined 1% to US$3,023.50, while nickel gave up 0.6% after surging 3.7% in the prior session on the prospect of coordinated output cuts by Chinese producers in Indonesia.

Iron ore fell as much as 1.7% to US$89.45 a tonne in Singapore, the lowest in almost two years.
